description:
Creates a timed meeting agenda — a shareable countdown timer that walks attendees through timeboxed topics in sync. Use when the user wants a meeting timer, timeboxes, a run of show, a workshop or standup schedule, or to keep a meeting on time. Not for calendar scheduling or note-taking, and a two-item chat needs no timer.

Returns share_token (what later calls take), share_url (the read-only live timer for attendees, safe to post anywhere) and edit_url (the private control page: start, pause, advance and finish the meeting, and edit blocks by hand). Without a linked BriefMe account it also returns edit_token, which later calls take instead of an account. The user needs both links.

When the blocks depart from BriefMe's standard shape — an opening, a wrap-up, planned breaks — the result also carries structure_suggestions, each naming the block to add and its length; add_block and reorder_blocks apply them.

Block durations add up to the meeting length; when none is given, a standup is about 15 minutes, a 1:1 about 30, sprint planning 60 to 90. Most agendas are three to eight blocks. Titles are read off a wall-sized countdown, so six words or fewer read best; a description is useful only when the title alone is ambiguous.

Include the opening, the wrap-up and any planned break in this first call: every change afterwards is a separate confirmation for the user.

Agendas expire after 7 days and cannot be recovered afterwards.

blocks.description: The agenda blocks, in the order they will run.

block_type.description: Internal classification for aggregate analysis, inferred from the content; shown on no BriefMe page.

description.description: Optional one-line note, only when the title is ambiguous.

duration_seconds.description: How long this block runs, in seconds.

title.description: Short, active, scannable on a countdown screen.

idempotency_key.description: Optional. Re-issuing a call with the same key and the same arguments returns the original result instead of repeating the change — send the same key when re-issuing a request whose response was lost. A fresh UUID per call works well; only a retry repeats one.

language.description: The user's conversation language as a two-letter ISO 639-1 code (e.g. 'de'). Localizes the standard block titles quoted in structure_suggestions. Unsupported values fall back to English. Defaults to the conversation locale the client sends (openai/locale) when omitted.

title.description: Short name for the meeting, e.g. "Weekly engineering sync".

name: create_agenda

blocks.description: The blocks in the order they run.

block_type.description: Internal classification; appears on no BriefMe page.

id.description: Stable 8-letter id: what update_block, remove_block, reorder_blocks and after_block_id take.

edit_token.description: What later anonymous calls take. Absent when the agenda is saved to a linked account.

edit_url.description: The private control page for running the meeting; not for a shared channel.

expires_at.description: ISO 8601. null when the agenda is saved to an account and does not expire.

instructions.description: What the user needs from this result.

share_token.description: The agenda's public identifier; what every tool takes as share_token.

share_url.description: The read-only agenda with the live timer; safe to give to attendees.

structure_suggestions.description: Present only when the agenda lacks an opening, a closing or a required break; add_block and reorder_blocks apply it.

title: Create a meeting agenda
